title: Caddy Web Server
wrapper_note:
the upstream image starts as root and keeps its configuration in root-owned
/etc/caddy. The entrypoint below keeps the user-editable Caddyfile in the
mounted application data directory, seeds a working default on the first start
and refuses to run an unusable Caddyfile (it falls back to a built-in default
instead of restarting in a loop).
wrapper_note_readme: - **Entrypoint wrapper**: the upstream image starts as root and reads its config from root-owned `/etc/caddy`, so the compose file replaces the entrypoint with `src/entrypoint.sh`. It seeds a working Caddyfile into the `config` volume on the first start, checks before starting that the file is parseable and really listens on container port 8080 (the one published port), and falls back to a built-in default when it is not, so a typo cannot take the application down or make it unreachable.
descript: Caddy is a powerful, open-source web server and reverse proxy with automatic HTTPS, written in Go. Serve your own website, and put any service running on your NAS or LAN behind a friendly path or host name - with one short configuration file. This app runs the official Docker Hub image as a non-root container and keeps the Caddyfile, your website files and the certificates in the application data folder, so nothing is lost on restart or update.
release_note: 1. First release: Caddy 2.11.4 from Docker Hub, running as a non-root container on your NAS. The Caddyfile and your website files live in the application data folder, a default site is created on the first start, and an unusable Caddyfile is replaced by a built-in default instead of breaking the app.
important: Requires DockerEngine (installed if missing); add a registry mirror if Docker Hub is unreachable. Open http://<NAS-IP>:8002/. Data lives in DockerAppData/caddydocker: Caddyfile in config, files in www, certificates in data. Apply edits with 'docker exec caddydocker caddy reload --config /config/Caddyfile'. Only port 8080 is published, so no automatic HTTPS for a public domain; a broken Caddyfile keeps the app on a built-in default. Back up the data folder before uninstalling with data removal.
data_notes: All state lives in the application data folder: `config/Caddyfile` is the configuration you edit, `www/` holds the files that are served, `data/` holds certificates and Caddy's runtime state, and `config/caddy/autosave.json` is Caddy's own copy of the running configuration.
design_notes: **Editable configuration in the data volume.** The upstream image keeps its Caddyfile in `/etc/caddy` and starts as root; the wrapper seeds it into `config/Caddyfile` instead, so it is editable from the NAS and survives application updates.

**An unusable Caddyfile cannot take the application down.** Before starting, the wrapper adapts the Caddyfile and requires a listener on container port 8080 (the only published port); on failure it starts with a built-in default. A typo therefore leaves the app reachable instead of causing a restart loop.
**No privileged port needed.** The container listens on 8080 and runs as uid 1000, so the app does not rely on the `cap_net_bind_service` file capability of the upstream image and needs no `cap_add`.
**Fixed image tag, never `:latest`**, Docker Hub only, no `privileged`, no `network_mode: host`, no Docker socket.
**Health check** probing the service on container port 8080.
limitations: Only one host port is published (8002). Automatic HTTPS for a public domain needs ports 80 and 443 and is therefore not available; use `tls internal` or your own certificate for TLS.
Sites have to listen on container port 8080 to be reachable. A Caddyfile that does not listen on 8080 is ignored and replaced by the built-in default site.
If you switch the published site to TLS on port 8080, the TOS health check (plain HTTP) may report the app as unhealthy even while it still serves HTTPS.
The default site is served over plain HTTP on the LAN. Do not expose the published port to the internet without TLS.

runtime_files.purpose: main configuration (sites, reverse proxies, TLS); seeded on the first start
Caddy's own copy of the running configuration (used by --resume)
runtime_files.lifecycle: managed by Caddy; do not edit

runtime_files.purpose: certificates, private keys, instance id and storage locks
runtime_files.growth: grows with the number of certificates
runtime_files.lifecycle: managed by Caddy; back it up to keep your certificates
never overwritten; replace it with your own site

zh-cn.descript: Caddy 是一款用 Go 编写、自带自动 HTTPS 的开源 Web 服务器与反向代理。你可以用它发布自己的网站，也可以把 NAS 或局域网里的任意服务放到好记的路径或域名后面，全部配置只需一个简短的 Caddyfile。本应用在 NAS 上以非 root 容器运行 Docker Hub 官方镜像，Caddyfile、网站文件与证书都保存在应用数据目录中，重启与更新都不会丢失。
zh-cn.important: 需要 DockerEngine（缺失时应用中心会自动提示安装）；若 NAS 无法直连 Docker Hub，请先在 DockerEngine 中配置镜像加速。安装后从 http://<NAS-IP>:8002/ 打开。本应用只发布一个端口，容器内 Caddy 监听 8080，因此无法为公网域名申请自动 HTTPS 证书，需要本地证书可用 'tls internal'。所有文件都在 DockerAppData/caddydocker 目录：配置在 config/Caddyfile， 网站文件在 www，证书在 data。改完配置用 'docker exec caddydocker caddy reload --config /config/Caddyfile' 热加载；Caddyfile 写错时应用会继续以内置默认配置运行，不会中断服务。卸载并删除数据前请先备份应用数据目录。
zh-cn.release_note: 1. 首次发布：来自 Docker Hub 的 Caddy 2.11.4，以非 root 容器运行。Caddyfile 与网站文件保存在应用数据目录，首次启动会生成默认站点；配置写错时会自动回退到内置默认配置，不会导致应用不可用。

zh-hk.descript: Caddy 是一款以 Go 撰寫、內建自動 HTTPS 的開源網頁伺服器與反向代理。你可以用它發佈自己的網站，也可以把 NAS 或區域網絡內的任何服務放到好記的路徑或網域後面，全部設定只需一個簡短的 Caddyfile。本應用在 NAS 上以非 root 容器執行 Docker Hub 官方映像，Caddyfile、網站檔案與憑證都保存在應用資料目錄中，重新啟動與更新都不會遺失。
zh-hk.important: 需要 DockerEngine（缺少時應用中心會自動提示安裝）；若 NAS 無法直連 Docker Hub，請先在 DockerEngine 中設定映像加速。安裝後從 http://<NAS-IP>:8002/ 開啟。本應用只發佈一個連接埠，容器內 Caddy 監聽 8080，因此無法為公網網域申請自動 HTTPS 憑證，需要本地憑證可用 'tls internal'。所有檔案都在 DockerAppData/caddydocker 目錄：設定在 config/Caddyfile， 網站檔案在 www，憑證在 data。改完設定用 'docker exec caddydocker caddy reload --config /config/Caddyfile' 熱載入；Caddyfile 寫錯時應用會繼續以內建預設設定執行，不會中斷服務。解除安裝並刪除資料前請先備份應用資料目錄。
zh-hk.release_note: 1. 首次發佈：來自 Docker Hub 的 Caddy 2.11.4，以非 root 容器執行。Caddyfile 與網站檔案保存在應用資料目錄，首次啟動會產生預設站台；設定寫錯時會自動回退到內建預設設定，不會導致應用無法使用。
